title: strrep
summary: Replace non-overlapping substring occurrences in text inputs with MATLAB-compatible container behavior.

gpu_support.notes: Replacement runs on host text. Numeric and provider-resident inputs are unsupported and reject before provider access.

description: `strrep(str, old, new)` replaces every non-overlapping occurrence of `old` with `new`. It supports MATLAB-compatible string, char, and cellstr-style inputs with element-wise replacement semantics.
behaviors: String scalars remain strings. Missing string values (`<missing>`) propagate unchanged.
String arrays are processed element-wise while preserving their full shape and orientation.
Character arrays are handled row by row. Rows expand or shrink as needed and are padded with spaces so the result stays a rectangular char array, just like MATLAB.
Cell arrays must contain character vectors or string scalars. The result is a cell array of identical size where each element has had the replacement applied.
The `old` and `new` arguments must be string scalars or character vectors of the same data type.
`old` can be empty. In that case, `strrep` inserts `new` before the first character, between existing characters, and after the final character.
Integer values in any of the three text roles are rejected rather than treated as character codes or formatted numbers.

examples.description: Replacing a word inside a string scalar
Updating every element of a string array
Preserving rectangular shape in character arrays
Applying replacements inside a cell array of character vectors
Inserting text with an empty search pattern
Converting numeric data explicitly before replacement

faqs.question: Which input types does `strrep` accept?
faqs.answer: String scalars, string arrays, character vectors, character arrays, and cell arrays of character vectors. The `old` and `new` arguments must be string scalars or character vectors of the same data type.

faqs.question: Does `strrep` support multiple search terms at once?
faqs.answer: No. Use the newer `replace` builtin if you need to substitute several search terms in a single call.

faqs.question: How does `strrep` handle missing strings?
faqs.answer: Missing string scalars remain `<missing>` and are returned unchanged, even when the search pattern matches ordinary text.

faqs.question: Will rows of a character array stay aligned?
faqs.answer: Yes. Each row is replaced individually, then padded with spaces so that the overall array stays rectangular, matching MATLAB exactly.

faqs.question: What happens when `old` is empty?
faqs.answer: RunMat mirrors MATLAB: `new` is inserted before the first character, between every existing character, and after the last character.

faqs.question: Does `strrep` run on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No GPU text representation is supported. Numeric GPU values are not text and reject before provider access; convert supported host data to strings explicitly before calling `strrep`.

faqs.question: Can I mix strings and character vectors for `old` and `new`?
faqs.answer: No. MATLAB requires `old` and `new` to share the same data type. RunMat enforces the same rule and raises a descriptive error when they differ.

faqs.question: How do I replace text stored inside cell arrays?
faqs.answer: `strrep` traverses the cell array, applying the replacement to each character vector or string scalar element and returning a cell array of the same shape.

gpu_residency: No. `strrep` accepts host text and returns host text. Provider-resident numeric values are unsupported and reject before access.
gpu_behavior: `strrep` computes replacements on host text and returns a host text container of the corresponding kind. Numeric resident values reject before provider access rather than being gathered and implicitly converted to text.
